blankElements.content:
She believed in enjoying the moment, loving people deeply, making memories, and never taking a day for granted. She had a big heart, a beautiful spirit, and a way of making everyone around her feel loved and welcome.
She was a woman of faith. Her relationship with God was an important part of who she was, and she found joy and fellowship in Bible study classes and in sharing her faith with others. She understood that life was a blessing, and she tried to live hers with gratitude, compassion, and purpose.
But perhaps her greatest joy of all was being a grandmother.
Her grandkids were her pride and joy. She loved watching them grow, celebrating their accomplishments, listening to their stories, and simply being there for them. Being “Granny” was more than a title to her—it was one of the greatest gifts of her life. Her grandchildren knew they were loved, supported, and cherished beyond measure. She was the kind of grandmother whose love could be felt in the smallest things: a conversation, a laugh, a favorite meal, a word of encouragement, or simply the comfort of knowing she was there.

Family meant everything to her. She treasured the time spent together and believed that some of life's best moments were made around the people you love. She also had a gift for friendship. Her family friends became like family, and the bonds she created throughout her life were genuine and lasting. She never met a stranger for long because her heart had a way of making room for everyone.
And she knew how to have a good time.
She loved to travel, make memories, and enjoy new experiences. One of her favorite adventures was going on cruises, where she could relax, laugh, enjoy good food, see new places, and spend time with the people she loved. She believed life was meant to be lived, and she made sure to enjoy it along the way.

blankElements.content:
She was a woman with a heart big enough for everyone. She gave love freely, cared deeply, and was always ready to offer a helping hand, a listening ear, or words of encouragement. She had a warmth about her that made people feel safe, valued, and at home.
Everything she touched was made better because of the love she poured into it. Every family gathering was a little warmer because she was there. Every friendship was richer because she was part of it. And every grandchild's life was brighter because they had the blessing of calling her Granny.
She leaves behind more than memories. She leaves behind lessons about faith, family, friendship, laughter, and making the most of every day. She leaves behind stories that will be told again and again, photographs that will bring smiles and tears, traditions that will continue, and a legacy of love that will live on through her children, grandchildren, family, and friends.
Though our hearts are broken that her time with us was not long enough, we are grateful for every moment we were given.
She lived her life loving God, loving her family, loving her friends, enjoying the journey, and making memories along the way.

Her grandkids were her pride and joy. 

Her family was her heart. Her faith was her foundation.

And her memory will forever be a blessing.

blankElements.content:
Dear Sweet Kaila,

Can't even find the words to say how empty we feel inside. You have been such a bright light in our lives. Your smile, your hugs (and sometimes pats), all of your beautiful creations of art and EVERYTHING about you will be missed.

"Trust in the Lord with all your heart and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge Him, and he will make your paths straight"
Proverbs 3:5-6

Oh how I will miss you, my Kaila. I will miss my kisses and your beautiful smile. You will always be my angel.

Love,
Olivia

You were a person that danced to the beat of your own drum. I listened to "The Dance" by Garth Brooks and it reminded me that I'm glad I didn't know the way it all would end, the way it all would go. Our lives are better left to chance I could have missed the pain, but I would have had to miss the dance, and believe me darling, you danced, everyday...you danced.

Love you,
DJ

We will FOREVER miss you and we will honor you always.

Love you so very much,
Kasei

Mom, we will miss your hugs, your laugh, your stories, the way you loved to sing and dance and “Step in the name of Love”. 

Mom, we’ll miss you more than words can say. But we take comfort knowing that your faith has brought you home, and that you are dancing in heaven right now with all of our loved ones who welcomed you with open arms. We love you,

Aunt Trisha, you were more than an aunt; you were a second mother to me. Your gentle smile, quiet demeanor, and kind heart made a difference in the lives of everyone around you. Thank you for loving me and my family unconditionally. You always listened and offered advice and encouragement without judgment.

You had a unique way of saying my name. You simply called me “Nessa,” spoken in a way that let me know I was exclusively your favored niece. You always made me feel special.

As Trisha’s health began to decline, I became her companion and caregiver. She was always my ride-or-die, the yin to my yang.

Mother, your love was pure. Your love was strong. Your love was unwavering.  You gave us a foundation of unconditional love that will stay with us forever.

Not only did you make sure we were rooted in love, but you also made sure we were rooted in faith. 
Your deep faith and love for the Lord was your anchor, guiding how you loved and treated everyone around you.
Though her journey on this earth has reached its horizon, her spirit echoes forever in my heart.

Aunt Trisha loved traveling back and forth to Port Arthur and watching Perry Mason and Gunsmoke. She also enjoyed sitting outside. My friends became her friends, and I will always remember her humor and hearty laugh whenever she joined in our conversations.

Even though I am overwhelmed with sadness as I reflect on the specific memories that made my relationship with my aunt so cherished, I know she embodied so much more. She was a role model to all, and I can proudly say that she left footprints in the sands of time.

Fare thee well, Auntie. You fought a good fight and won the race. You left a legacy that will be remembered for generations to come. As the matriarch of our family, you left a mark on our hearts that nothing will ever erase.
Surely, Auntie, our love for you will forever remain.
